info.name: Applicant Service
info.description:
Applicant Service — Team 16, "Student ID, please" (FAF.PAD21.1).

The service owns the identity of the people trying to get into the university Discord server. Every applicant exists twice: the profile they claim, which this API serves, and the profile that is true, which never leaves the service except inside the applicant.initialized event.

Run the requests top to bottom: "Next applicant" stores the new applicant_id in a collection variable, and the requests after it reuse it.

Set `base_url` to where the service is listening (http://localhost:8081 by default).

request.description: Answers 200 whenever the process is serving. It deliberately does not check Postgres: a liveness probe that fails on a dependency restarts a healthy container because somebody else is having a bad day.
Reports whether the service can do useful work. Postgres is the only hard dependency; without RabbitMQ the status is "degraded" and events queue in the outbox until it returns.

item.name: Through the Gateway
item.description: In the running system nothing calls Applicant Service directly: every request enters at the Gateway as `{{gateway_url}}/api/v1/applicant/...`, which checks the credential, removes it and forwards the rest to the service's `/api/v1/...` (CPR README, Gateway and Authentication). A service call carries `X-Service-Token`; a player's carries `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`, which this folder's pre-request script mints for `player_id` with `jwt_secret`. `service_token` and `jwt_secret` must match the Gateway's SERVICE_TOKEN and JWT_SECRET, and the Gateway must reach the service as APPLICANT_URL. The policy per route is the Gateway's; the service itself checks no credential and reads only `X-Player-Id`.

exec: // Player tokens, signed the way Player Service signs them: HS256 with JWT_SECRET, `sub` = the
// player's id, `iat` and `exp`. The Gateway verifies the signature, so `jwt_secret` must be the
// JWT_SECRET of the Gateway being called (gateway-service/.env).
return header + '.' + payload + '.' + b64url(CryptoJS.HmacSHA256(header + '.' + payload, secret));
pm.collectionVariables.set('player_token', mint({ sub: sub, iat: now, exp: now + 3600 }, secret));

request.description: `/api/v1/applicant/health` is forwarded to the service's `/health`: a public route, no credential, not counted as a task. The Gateway adds `X-Request-ID` when the caller sent none.
Readiness leaks dependency state, so the Gateway forwards it only with the service token; without one it answers 403 SERVICE_TOKEN_REQUIRED.

How Server Moderation Session Service calls it: `POST {gateway}/api/v1/applicant/applicants/next` with the shared `X-Service-Token`. The Gateway forwards it as `POST /api/v1/applicants/next` without the token, and never retries it, so an applicant is never created twice.
